Enjoy figuring out how the data fits together? 
 An unfamiliar database, a tricky conversion, a migration ready to run. If that sounds like your kind of work, we’d like to hear from you!
 We’re looking for an Intermediate ETL Developer to join Pandell-ESG's Project Services team. You’ll help customers move their data into our software and work alongside a strong team that’s ready to roll up their sleeves and help.
 About the role 
 You’ll work through the details of each migration: understanding the customer’s data, planning how it needs to be converted, and writing the scripts to make it happen. You’ll learn different data models, adapt our conversion tools, and troubleshoot along the way.
 You’ll also have opportunities to take the technical lead on small to medium-sized projects and help other team members build their skills and confidence. It’s a role for someone who enjoys hands-on technical work and wants to take on more responsibility with a team behind them.
 Your team 
 Our Project Services team helps customers implement software across Pandell’s suite of more than 12 product groups. You’ll work with colleagues who understand the software and the business processes behind it, sharing ideas, and working through challenges together.
 About Us: 
 ESG, along with its subsidiary Pandell, is a global leader in energy software, providing Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions that support companies across utilities, renewables, retail energy, and oil and gas.
 Across North America and the UK, our combined platforms help teams manage key parts of their business, including billing, asset management, regulatory requirements, and geospatial data. These tools bring together the information and workflows teams rely on every day, making it easier to run operations and stay organized.
 Through cloud-based technology and data-driven insights, we help energy companies navigate complex markets and continue progressing toward Net-Zero goals.
 Life at Pandell-ESG 
 We care about doing good work and being good people to work with. That means making room for questions, listening to different perspectives, and helping each other when the work gets complicated.
 We want people to feel welcome, respected, and comfortable being themselves. You’ll have the trust, tools, and flexibility to do your work, along with support from your teammates.
 What you'll do: 
 Plan data migrations, turning project requirements into a technical approach.
 Write and run conversion scripts to move data between systems.
 Develop tools and make changes to our conversion frameworks to meet project needs.
 Get to know customers’ data and business processes, working through unfamiliar data models with support from senior teammates.
 Take the technical lead on small to medium-sized projects, helping plan the work, estimate effort, and keep technical tasks on track.
 Review code and test other developers’ work, with guidance when needed, to check that it meets project requirements and team standards.
 Troubleshoot issues during development, configuration, and performance tuning.
 Keep technical documentation clear and accurate, and talk through technical questions with colleagues.
 Help other developers build their skills and confidence through mentoring and feedback.
 What you’ll bring 
 5+ years of hands-on experience working with SQL, SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS), and Oracle databases.
 Experience writing complex queries and data conversion scripts, with a solid understanding of database tables and how they relate to one another.
 Knowledge of T-SQL, PL/SQL, C#, and PowerShell for ETL scripting and tool development.
 Experience with ETL processes, data migrations, and conversion frameworks, including writing and running scripts of moderate complexity.
 Experience building tools and making changes to existing frameworks.
 An understanding of relational and non-relational databases.
 Familiarity with the software development life cycle and how it applies to data conversion, configuration, and deployment.
 The ability to guide technical work on a project and review code against requirements and quality standards.
 Good judgement when planning your work, estimating how long tasks will take, and managing competing deadlines.
 Clear communication, attention to detail, and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
 Curiosity about unfamiliar systems and an interest in continuing to learn.
 Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related technical field.
 Bonus points for: 
 Experience with Visual Studio, Microsoft Access, Excel, GitHub, Jira, or TeamCity.
 Knowledge of the energy industry, particularly land administration or land management.
 We’d love to see your work. If you have a GitHub profile or code samples you’re able to share, include a link with your application.
 What’s In It for You? 
 At Pandell-ESG, we believe in  creating a workplace where you can do your best work  while enjoying  meaningful projects and a strong sense of belonging . 
 Here are just a few things we offer:
 Work-from-home or office flexibility - choose where you work best!
 Flexible hours to support work-life balance 
 Competitive benefits package, including 100% dental reimbursement 
 Retirement Savings Plan with company matching 
 Training budget and professional development opportunities 
 Fully stocked kitchen at the office with healthy options, snacks, and plenty of coffee 
 A fun and engaging culture with virtual and in-person events, learning opportunities, and a games room and lounge 
 A wellness budget to support your version of wellbeing
 Join us and be part of something EPIC. 
 If you’re excited about helping customers succeed, bringing software to life through training , and collaborating with an incredible team , we’d love to hear from you!
 Apply today and let’s Craft the Future of Energy Software together

See what you can do with Prophix 
 At Prophix, we’re building the platform that helps finance teams stop managing spreadsheets and start driving strategy. Prophix One™ brings planning, reporting, consolidation, and automation together in a single place, and we are expanding its AI capabilities faster than ever. If you want to work on a product that genuinely changes how finance teams operate, and do it alongside people who care about getting it right, this is where you want to be. 
 We’re headquartered in the Greater Toronto Area, with teams and offices across North America, Europe, and Australia. Trusted by more than 3,000 finance teams across 100+ countries, Prophix One™ is built for organisations that want to plan smarter and move faster.
 As the Manager of Product Training & Enablement, you will shape how Prophix's employees and customers learn, designing and delivering product training solutions that build capability and drive performance. You'll work closely with stakeholders across specific business units, new hires, and customers to build learning programs that are engaging, measurable, and aligned to where the business is headed. This is a role for someone who believes great learning experiences can change outcomes and wants the ownership to prove it.
 What You Will Do 
 Own the Learning Strategy and Roadmap 
 · Design and own a comprehensive learning strategy covering new hires, tenured Phixers, customers, and partners, segmented by audience and prioritized against Prophix’s business goals, reviewed and adjusted as those goals shift
 · Build and maintain the enablement roadmap for global Customer Experience programs, including support for EMEA and LATAM as Prophix’s footprint grows
 · Proactively partner across Professional Services, Customer Success, Product Adoption, and Support to identify learning gaps before they show up as support tickets or stalled adoption
 Design and Deliver Training People Actually Want to Sit Through 
 · Apply instructional design methodology to build learning experiences for new hires, tenured Phixers, customers, and partners, tailored to how each audience actually learns, not a one-size-fits-all deck
 · Personally facilitate product training sessions, virtually and in person, bringing subject-matter depth and genuinely engaging delivery to every session
 · Own Prophix Live and other recurring customer training programs end to end, content, scheduling, and how sessions are communicated and promoted to customers
 · Own partner training and enablement, since partner delivery depends on programs built and maintained by this function
 · Build and maintain training content (course materials, live demos, job aids) that’s accurate, practical, and designed to be interactive rather than passive
 Measure What’s Working, Then Act On It 
 · Define and track success metrics across all learning programs, and use the data, attendance, completion, support ticket trends, satisfaction, to find what’s actually breaking down, not just report that it is
 · Bring a builder’s mindset to every program: if something isn’t landing, redesign it rather than running it as-is out of habit
 Lead the Team and Scale the Function With AI 
 · Lead and coach a small team of Learning and Content Specialists, setting clear expectations and giving them real project ownership
 · Embed AI-powered tools across the learning function for content creation, personalized learning paths, data analysis, and generating new ideas and formats, not just making existing ones faster
 · Stay current on L&D and AI trends, and champion a culture of learning, collaboration, and compliance (including DEI principles) across the teams you support
 What You Will Bring 
 We hire for potential as much as experience. If this role excites you but you don’t check every box, we still want to hear from you. At Prophix, people who ask good questions, adapt quickly, and bring a fresh perspective often make the biggest impact.
 Required Qualifications 
 · Post-secondary education in Adult Learning, Instructional Design, Organizational Development, or a related discipline, supplemented by facilitation or training certifications.
 · 5+ years of experience in SaaS learning and development, with a demonstrated track record of designing and delivering impactful learning solutions (product training for both external and internal stakeholders)
 · 2+ years leading or mentoring a team of learning or content professionals, with the ability to set clear expectations, coach on delivery quality, and give people real ownership of their programs
 · Solid understanding of instructional design methodologies and the ability to customize them for diverse audiences, including customers, new hires, and tenured employees
 ·  Hands-on experience with learning technologies (e.g., AI tools, Skilljar, or 360 Learning) and a genuine interest in using them to create engaging, modern learning experiences
 · Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to measure program effectiveness and translate data into meaningful improvements
 · Excellent stakeholder management and collaboration skills, with a proven ability to build relationships and align across teams and business units
 · Comfortable using AI tools to drive efficiency and continuous improvement
 · Outstanding communication and presentation skills, with confidence facilitating learning experiences for varied audiences
 · Willingness and ability to travel approximately 10% of the time
 · Must be legally entitled to work in Canada
 Preferred Qualifications 
 · Experience developing customer-facing, partner or channel enablement training programs within a B2B SaaS environment
 · Prior experience in a CPM, FP&A, or other financial software company 
 · Experience applying AI tools specifically to learning content creation or personalized learning paths
 · Experience building or supporting global training programs for distributed, multi-region audiences (e.g., EMEA, LATAM)
 · Naturally curious and proactive mindset, someone who challenges the status quo and continuously seeks better ways to meet the needs of a growing global organization
 What Success Looks Like 
 30 days: You know the platform, the team, and the current state of every active learning program enough to see what's working and what isn't.
 90 days: You've published a stakeholder-validated learning strategy and roadmap, and built real working relationships with Professional Services, Customer Success, Product Adoption, and Support, a jointly owned plan, not just introductions.
 6-12 months: You've redesigned or built a customer-facing training program that's measurably moved the needle — fewer repeat support tickets, better completion and satisfaction scores — and your team has clear expectations and real ownership of their work.
 Why Join Prophix? 
 Prophix is headquartered in the GTA, so joining our team puts you close to where decisions are made, strategy is set, and careers are built. You’ll collaborate across North America, Europe, and Australia, developing breadth you simply can’t get at a single market company. Our people move across functions, work directly with customers in different industries, and take on meaningful challenges early.  We’re a company that competes on talent. That means we invest in the people who show up curious, move fast, and want to leave things better than they found them. Our values are Pursue Excellence, Build with Purpose, Create Wins for All, and Drive Continuous Innovation, and they guide how we actually make decisions.   
 Compensation 
 The total target compensation for this role is $110,000 CAD to $120,000 CAD, in accordance with applicable pay transparency laws. Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as skills, experience, location, and internal equity.  
 What’s Included for You? 
 · Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and mental-health coverage 
 · Retirement savings with employer contributions 
 · Parental leave top-up 
 · Annual wellness allowance 
 · Generous paid time off including vacation and sick time 
 · Social events, team activities, and opportunities to build community 
 · Opportunities to participate in Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives 
 · Quarterly Town Halls and Kickoffs that bring teams together to celebrate wins, share updates, and look ahead at what’s next
 Apply Now! 
 If you’re looking for a place where your work touches real products, real customers, and real decisions, and where your career can grow in the direction you choose. We would love to meet you. Apply and let’s talk about what’s possible.  
 Accessibility & AI Transparency 
 Prophix promotes an accessible hiring process. If you need accommodation at any stage, we’ll work with you. Some interviews may be recorded so our hiring team can review and assess responses fairly and consistently. As part of our commitment to Responsible AI, we use a small number of AI-supported tools to help with tasks like resume review, shortlisting, or creating interview summaries. AI is never used as the sole basis for hiring decisions, and your personal data is never used to train AI models. If you'd prefer not to take part in any AI-assisted step, just let us know and we’ll be happy to accommodate.

Tenstorrent is leading the industry on cutting-edge AI technology, revolutionizing performance expectations, ease of use, and cost efficiency. With AI redefining the computing paradigm, solutions must evolve to unify innovations in software models, compilers, platforms, networking, and semiconductors. Our diverse team of technologists have developed a high performance RISC-V CPU from scratch, and share a passion for AI and a deep desire to build the best AI platform possible. We value collaboration, curiosity, and a commitment to solving hard problems. We are growing our team and looking for contributors of all seniorities.
 Our Tensix team is building custom AI compute cores, RISC-V CPUs, and chiplet-based architectures for datacenter, edge, and automotive AI. Design Verification Engineers on this team validate compute IP and subsystems and build scalable DV infrastructure to keep verification fast, automated, and production-grade.
 This role is hybrid, based out of Toronto, ON, Austin, TX or Belgrade, Serbia.
 We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.
 Who You Are 
 Experienced in modern verification methodologies with strong SystemVerilog skills and exposure to structured testbench development.
 Comfortable working from block-level to system-level verification and reasoning about microarchitecture behavior from specs and waveforms.
 Proficient in Linux environments with Python, or Bash scripting for automate builds, parse logs, manage CI pipelines.
 Skilled in coverage-driven verification and confident debugging across RTL, testbench, and workload scenarios.
 Motivated by AI hardware and eager to learn verification strategies for new architectures and domains.
 What We Need 
 Contribute to verification of Tensix IP and subsystems from early planning through tape-out, owning coverage goals and driving them to closure.
 Build and maintain reusable verification environments, agents, scoreboards, and supporting infrastructure in SystemVerilog and Python.
 Develop constrained-random and directed tests and close functional, code, and assertion coverage using data-driven approaches.
 Debug complex issues across RTL and testbench while collaborating with design, firmware, compiler, and architecture teams.
 Help evolve DV infrastructure including regression flows, CI/CD integration, EDA compute environments, and reproducible setups.
 Nice to have: Exposure to functional safety (FuSa) verification concepts for automotive AI workloads.
 Nice to have: Familiarity with formal verification methodologies, SVA (SystemVerilog Assertions), or formal property verification for complex control logic and microarchitectural corner cases.
 What You Will Learn 
 How Tenstorrent verifies AI-native compute architectures including Tensix cores, RISC-V CPUs, matrix units, vector units, and datapath.
 How simulation, emulation, and software-driven workloads combine to validate both functional correctness and performance.
 How numerical precision formats such as BF16, FP4, and INT8 and on-chip dataflow impact verification complexity and coverage strategy.
 How to build scalable DV infrastructure across hybrid compute environments including containerized regression systems.
 How data analytics and modern AI tooling can enhance verification workflows and accelerate convergence.

This is a hybrid role that can be performed three days per week from our Ottawa office. 
 Meet the Team 
Acacia designs intelligent transceivers using advanced signal processing and photonic integration for the 100G, 400G, 800G and 1.6T+ bit speed fiber optic transmission market deployed in data center, metro, long-haul and ultra-long haul telecommunication networks.
You will work with other Acacia mixed-signal engineers to collaborate in order to provide an optimized design that will integrate into the ASIC. In addition, you will have the opportunity to interact with other Acacia groups including digital/DSP design, system design, package design, and module design. Acacia takes pride in providing and fostering a collaborate environment in order ensure success and personal growth.
 Your Impact 
As a senior member of the Mixed Signal Design team, you will be a key member of a small, dynamic IC Design group that develops high speed (>25Gb/s), and high accuracy, analog designs for optical communications products. You will architect, design, layout, measure and productize ultra-deep sub-micron-based CMOS products.
 You will lead efforts for a large block on a complex chip, mentor team members and track deliverables, participate in peer review of complex IC designs and provide solid design methodology from conception to production.
 You will also collaborate with packaging and hardware design team to ensure signal and power integrity specifications are met.
 You are enthusiastic about developing high speed AMS circuits and best-in-class products that push the boundaries of what is possible. You are detail oriented, high energy and the drive to get things done and solve difficult problems.
 You are capable to figure things out by yourself, but you also participate in our friendly and team-oriented collaboration approach, which means you enjoy learning from your colleagues and letting them learn from you.
 You are not shy to always point out how we can be more effective as a team, and you are open to similar suggestions by your team members.
 Minimum Qualification 
 Bachelors + 12 years of related experience, or Masters + 8 years of related experience, or PhD + 5 years of related experience.
 Prior experience in the design, simulation, and measurement of high-speed ICs across at least three of the following areas: SerDes/serial links, output drivers, Phase Locked Loops (PLLs), clock distribution, Opamps/PGAs, or equalization techniques.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience with electrical transceiver applications including backplane and cable communications.
 Experience in FinFET and GAA technologies.
 High-frequency layout experience including floorplaning (power/ground, digital/analog signal routing), passives components (inductors, transformers, and transmission-lins).
 Experience in design for manufacturability including characterization over PVT, electromigration analysis, self-heating, and IR drop analysis.
 Experience in laboratory validation including ESD practices/methodology and construction of test setups.
 Experience in design software including Cadence (Virtuoso), Specture/APS/SpectreX, layout validation tools (Virtuoso and Calibre), EMX, mixed-signal simulations in AMS, and Matlab.

Acacia, qui fait partie de Cisco, fournit des produits d'interconnexion optique haute vitesse à base de silicium innovants qui accélèrent l'évolutivité du réseau grâce à des avancées en matière de rendement, de capacité et de coûts. Nos circuits ASIC DSP, nos circuits intégrés photoniques sur silicium et nos modules cohérents permettent aux fournisseurs de services cloud et de services de répondre à la demande croissante de données. Nous avons réuni une équipe d'experts interfonctionnels capables de relever les défis liés aux interconnexions optiques de nouvelle génération, ce qui se traduit par des produits primés à la fine pointe de la technologie. Venez vous joindre à Cisco, qui a été désigné comme l'un des meilleurs lieux de travail au monde, et effectuer un travail porteur de sens qui a une incidence mondiale et qui contribue à une culture d'entreprise favorisant un avenir inclusif pour tous.
Vous collaborerez avec d'autres ingénieurs de signaux mixtes d'Acacia afin de fournir une conception optimisée qui s'intégrera dans le circuit ASIC. De plus, vous aurez l'occasion d'interagir avec d'autres groupes Acacia, notamment dans la conception numérique/DSP, la conception de systèmes, la conception du conditionnement et la conception de modules. Acacia est fière de fournir et de favoriser un environnement de collaboration afin d'assurer la réussite et l'épanouissement personnel.Vos fonctions :
En tant que membre principal de l'équipe de conception de signaux mixtes, vous serez un membre clé d'un petit groupe de conception de circuits intégrés dynamique qui développe des conceptions analogiques à haute vitesse  (> 25 Gb/s) et de haute précision pour les produits de communications optiques.
Vous serez en charge de l'architecture, de la conception, de la disposition, de la mesure et de la commercialisation de produits CMOS ultra-profonds submicroniques.
 Vous dirigerez les efforts portant sur un bloc important d'une puce complexe, encadrerez les membres de l'équipe et assurerez le suivi des livrables, participerez à l'examen par les pairs des conceptions de circuits intégrés complexes et fournirez une méthodologie de conception solide, de la conception à la production.
 Vous collaborerez également avec l'équipe de conception du conditionnement et du matériel pour vous assurer que les spécifications d'intégrité du signal et de l'alimentation sont respectées.
 Vous avez de la passion par le développement de circuits AMS à haute vitesse et de produits de pointe qui repoussent les limites du possible. Vous avez le souci du détail, vous avez beaucoup d'énergie et vous avez la volonté de faire avancer les choses et de résoudre des problèmes difficiles.
 Vous êtes capable de trouver des solutions par vous-même, mais vous participez également à notre approche de collaboration conviviale et axée sur le travail d'équipe, ce qui signifie que vous aimez apprendre de vos collègues et leur permettre d'apprendre de vous.

 Qualifications Minimales 
 Baccalauréat et 12 ans d’expérience connexe, ou maîtrise et de 6 ans d’expérience connexe, ou doctorat et au moins 3 ans d’expérience connexe.
 Expérience préalable dans la conception, la simulation et la mesure de circuits intégrés haute vitesse dans au moins trois des domaines suivants : liaisons SerDes/série, circuits d'attaque de sortie, boucles à verrouillage de phase (PLL), distribution d'horloge, amplificateurs opérationnels/PGA ou techniques d'égalisation.
 Qualifications Recherchées 
 Expérience dans les applications de transmetteurs-récepteurs électriques, notamment les communications par fond de panier et par câble.
 Expérience avec les technologies FinFET et GAA.
 Expérience du plan de masse des hautes fréquences, y compris l'agencement (alimentation et mise à la terre, routage des signaux numériques et analogiques), les composants passifs (inductances, transformateurs et lignes de transmission).
 Expérience de la conception axée sur la fabricabilité, y compris la caractérisation selon les variations PVT, l'analyse de l'électromigration, de l'auto-échauffement et de la chute de tension IR.
 Expérience de la validation en laboratoire, y compris les pratiques et la méthodologie relatives aux décharges électrostatiques et la construction de configurations d'essai.
 Expérience des logiciels de conception, notamment Cadence (Virtuoso), Spectre/APS/SpectreX, des outils de validation de la disposition (Virtuoso et Calibre), EMX, des simulations de signaux mixtes dans AMS et Matlab.

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


Role Overview:

As a Member of Technical Staff in the Safety for Agents team, you will make a meaningful impact on the development of better, fairer, more trustworthy, and more secure Large Language Models (LLMs). Your primary focus will be on data generation, post-training algorithms, and evaluation methods to ensure Safety in the next generation of models that can access external resources and take actions in the world. You will work closely with other cross-functional machine learning teams and data annotation teams, and will also collaborate with product and policy teams.

This role combines expertise in machine learning, ethical and responsible AI, experimental design, and data generation and management.

It will require curiosity to tackle totally new scientific problems, engineering skills to implement the pieces we need to test solutions to these, and a desire to dive into messy data and results. You will be on a small team with a lot of autonomy and decision-making power, responsible for making the next generation of LLMs better for society as a whole.



Please Note: The existing team work in offices in London, Edinburgh, Paris, Toronto, and New York, but we also embrace being remote-friendly! For this role you need to have ~50% working day overlap with UK/EU timezone (e.g. US East is fine) but there are otherwise no restrictions on where you can be located for this role.

Key responsibilities:

 - Strong statistical skills and experience evaluating scientific experiments related to data collection and model performance.

 - Extremely strong software engineering skills.

 - Strong expertise in designing and conducting data collection tasks, including working with human annotators.

 - Experience analyzing datasets with respect to their quality, biases, and suitability for training ML models.

 - Hands-on experience training large language models (LLMs) on distributed training infrastructures.

 - Familiarity with evaluating and improving the generalizability and robustness of ML systems.

 - Proficiency in programming languages such as Python and ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX).

 - Excellent communication skills to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams and present findings.

 - One or more papers at top-tier venues (such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AIStats, MLSys, JMLR, AAAI, Nature, COLING, ACL, EMNLP).



Working Location:
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.





FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.



We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.



Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

 The Academic Services Coordinator provides a broad spectrum of responsibilities including but not limited to client service, academic integrity, calendar management, support for core functions (e.g., admissions, First Year Engineering Office, etc.), special projects, data management, and general administrative duties. The position acts as a liaison with academic units in the Faculty of Engineering and central university services as it relates to key accountabilities. Reporting to one of the Associate Directors, the Academic Services Coordinator provides exceptional client support for 14 undergraduate programs and approximately 8,000 plus Engineering and Architecture students. The role moves seamlessly between tasks, shifting priorities as directed by Director, Undergraduate Affairs and the Associate Dean, Undergraduate Studies, to address critical needs. The Academic Services Coordinator provides continuity in leadership changes and demonstrates breadth and depth in all core operations in the Engineering Undergraduate Studies Office. 
 Key Accountabilities 
 Client Service: 
 Builds and maintains effective working relationships with stakeholders within the Faculty and across campus. 
 Provides exceptional client service to all constituents within the Faculty of Engineering (students, faculty, and staff), including acting as a liaison with central services and external partners. 
 Acts as a liaison for academic units. Duties may include several key areas including academic integrity, calendar management, admissions, data management, general administrative support, etc. The incumbent is expected to shift seamlessly between tasks to address priority areas. 
 Develops strong advising relationships that are student-centred and specific to individual needs while aligning with the mission of the Faculty. 
 Assists stakeholders with identifying and accessing tools and resources necessary to meet goals and objectives. 
 Applies change management expertise with new stakeholders and various audiences 
 Cultivates relationships built on trust with individuals in one-on-one and online environments, focusing on the values and needs of the client group while encouraging self-efficacy, resilience, and career potential. 
 Facilitates group learning opportunities through workshops, presentations, events, and resources to meet client needs. 
 Supports the development and implementation of best practice for student-centred services across the faculty. 
 Specific Accountabilities: 
 The Academic Services Coordinator is expected to support several key accountabilities including but not limited to : 
 Student Experience Administration – Provides a welcoming experience by delivering exceptional service in a student-centered environment. The incumbent is expected to work within established standards and best practice. The Academic Services Coordinator contributes to the development of resources to support the student experience in the Engineering Undergraduate Studies Office through direct interaction with students visiting the office, enhanced websites, online forms, appointment booking sites, virtual advising. The incumbent supports several key events including Teaching Assistant Workshops, accreditation and external site visits, Iron Ring ceremony, presentations, workshops, and stakeholder visits (e.g., Professional Engineers Ontario). 
 Academic Advisement – The primary responsibilities of the advisor are to provide academic advice and support to first year engineering students, maintain student database records, and review academic progression reports. To accomplish these tasks, the advisor must have a strong understanding of the academic expectations for each of the engineering programs as well as the academic regulations within the Faculty of Engineering. The advisor will participate in initiatives to enhance the student experience. The advisor will offer academic support to students when non academic issues (personal, medical, financial, etc.) affect the student’s academic experience. 
 Exchange  – Works in conjunction with multiple stakeholders across the Faculty of Engineering, Student Success Office (SSO) and the Registrar’s Office. Liaises between department personnel and the SSO to ensure a streamlined outbound and inbound exchange experience. Participates in the exchange community of practice with representatives from across the six faculties. Supports current undergraduate students seeking information about exchange opportunities. Supports international students studying in the Faculty of Engineering on undergraduate exchange. Administers Faculty of Engineering exchange processes including, but not limited to, the reconciliation of student records, student eligibility and endorsement, and program compatibility with alternate school curriculum. 
 Accreditation – Provides support to various committees on matters relating to co-operative education and accreditation (CEAB). The incumbent maintains data on professional licensing and registration, supports the planning and logistics for visits by external reviewers and acts as a liaison with academic units. 
 Communications – Works in conjunction with multiple stakeholders within the Engineering Undergraduate Studies Office to develop communications as it relates to recruitment, admissions, calendar management, academic integrity, policy and best practice. The incumbent is responsible for developing and delivering consistent, professional, and creative internal communications to engage students, faculty, and staff through written communication pieces, websites, social media and other digital communication tools. 
 Academic Integrity Management – Promotes and facilitates an environment that focuses on academic integrity. The incumbent advises students, instructors and staff on academic integrity matters and academic misconduct. The Academic Services Coordinator is responsible for educating and informing students, faculty, and staff on issues related to academic integrity through facilitated and non-facilitated workshops and seminars. The incumbent acts as an expert resource and provides information on relevant policies and process. The Academic Services Coordinator is responsible for academic offence cases within the Faculty of Engineering ensuring files are appropriately and accurately managed to completion. 
 Undergraduate Calendar Management – Oversees academic regulations, policies, and updates the undergraduate calendar ensuring the successful delivery of the undergraduate program. The incumbent provides leadership in the adoption, standardization of data, tools, techniques, development and implementation of policies and procedures related to the undergraduate curriculum in partnership with academic units. The Academic Services Coordinator participates on internal committees and special projects as it relates to the undergraduate curriculum. 
 Support for Special Projects  – The Academic Services Coordinator provides expert support on special projects and strategic initiatives as directed by leadership. The incumbent participates in and contributes to discussions on special projects consistent with the Faculty’s strategic priorities including enhancing student experience. The Academic Services Coordinator may be required to consult with key stakeholders to understand diverse needs. 
 Support for Core Functions – The Academic Services Coordinator operates as part of larger team contributing to various core functions in Engineering Undergraduate Studies. Duties may include administrative support and event planning for activities in the First Year Engineering Office during peak times, supporting the recruitment and admissions process, etc. The incumbent may be required to support advising, scheduling, etc. as needed to ensure efficiency in operations. 
 Data Collection and Management  – The incumbent supports the facilitation of data integration across programs. The Academic Services Coordinator supports senior leadership on a variety of data needs including but not limited to data collection, management, and warehousing. The incumbent provides input on system limitations, participates in the planning and implementation of new platforms.

 Supports the activities of the Associate Dean, Undergraduate Studies, and other senior leadership. 
 Serves as a resource for the application of policies, procedures, guidelines, and best practice. 
 Contributes to the enhancement of student-centred service models. 
 Contributes to the development of various reports, presentations, communications, etc.

 Experience

You turn scrollers into followers… and followers into customers. You know how to make people stop, watch, follow, click… and buy. Likes are nice. Views are nice. But sales are nicer. Because great organic social doesn’t just build an audience. It earns attention, builds trust, and turns that trust into measurable revenue.
 If that sounds like you, you might have what it takes to become our next Organic Social Specialist. 
 Small Print ⇒ We’re not looking for a “like junkie.” We want someone who knows how to grow a social audience and turn that attention into sales. Someone who understands that followers, views, and engagement are only useful if they build trust, drive traffic, and ultimately help customers buy. If you measure success by views alone then this probably isn’t the role for you.
 Still here?
 Okay then…
 This job will give you ALL the feels: 
 We create clinically supported, natural solutions for some of the biggest health challenges women over 40 face today. And your work will help more women discover those solutions. You’ll help us become a brand these women actually want to follow. You’ll help create the posts that make her stop. The videos she sends to a friend. The content that makes her think, “Finally. Someone actually gets it.”
 If that excites you, you’ll find no better place to continue your career than here.
 This job might be for you if… 
 You understand what makes people stop scrolling . Hooks. Thumbnails. First frames. Captions. Curiosity. Emotion. Pattern interrupts. Trends. You don’t need someone to explain why the first two seconds of a TikTok matter. You already spend more time than is probably healthy wondering why one piece of content gets 327 views while another gets 327,000.
 You know every platform speaks a slightly different language. TikTok isn’t Instagram. Instagram isn’t Facebook. YouTube isn’t Reddit. And taking the exact same post, resizing it four times, and calling it a “social strategy” makes a small part of you die inside. You know how to adapt an idea to the platform, audience, format, and reason somebody is there in the first place.
 You can actually create the stuff. We’re not looking for someone who just sits in meetings talking about content pillars. You’ll help develop ideas, write briefs, schedule content, coordinate assets, get everything live, and make sure the little details don’t fall through the cracks.
 You’ve got a nose for a good trend. Sounds. Formats. Memes. Conversations. Creators. Questions people suddenly can’t stop asking. You pay attention to what’s happening online and can tell the difference between a trend we should jump on… and one that will make a women’s health company look like someone’s dad discovered TikTok.
 You’re obsessed with the audience. What are women talking about? What are they frustrated by? What are they asking in the comments? What myths keep popping up? What are competitors saying? What language are real women actually using? You know some of the best content ideas won’t come from a brainstorm. They’ll come from listening.
 You care about results more than vanity metrics. Followers and likes are lovely. But you also want to know what people clicked, what sent traffic to the site, what converted, what content assisted a sale, and what we should do differently next month. Because ultimately, we’re not trying to win a trophy for “nicest Instagram grid.”
 Numbers don’t make your eyes glaze over. Reach. Engagement. Clicks. Conversion. Follower growth. Traffic. UTMs. GA4. You don’t have to be a data scientist wearing six monitors and muttering about statistical significance. But you should be able to look at performance, spot patterns, and turn what you learn into better content.
 You know how to use social scheduling tools without needing an emergency tutorial. Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Later, Buffer, or something similar. We don’t care which logo you’ve stared at most. We care that you understand how to plan, schedule, organize, and manage a social calendar without everything descending into chaos.
 You can turn performance into strategy. You don’t just send a monthly report containing 17 charts and the groundbreaking observation that “engagement was up.” You ask why. What worked? What flopped? Which topics got attention? Which formats drove clicks? What should we do more of? Less of? Test next? The report is only useful if it changes what we do.
 You’re organised enough to keep a lot of little moving pieces moving. Content calendars. Briefs. Designers. Video. Approvals. Links. UTMs. Scheduling. Launch dates. Reporting. Somebody has to keep track of it all. Preferably without sending 14 Slack messages asking, “Any update on this?”
 You play nicely with others. You’ll work with Content, Creative, Acquisition, Email, Influencer, Customer Service and other teams across the business. Sometimes you’ll need something from them. Sometimes they’ll need something from you. You communicate clearly, follow up, solve problems, and understand that being easy to work with is a genuine career superpower.
 You know social never stops changing . Algorithm updates. New features. New formats. Social commerce. Search behaviour. Yesterday’s “best practice” suddenly dying a very public death. You’re curious enough to keep learning without somebody having to chase you around the office waving an industry newsletter.
 You’ve got at least a year of experience in social media marketing or something closely related. Maybe you’ve managed brand accounts. Maybe you’ve built social for an ecommerce company. Maybe you’ve helped grow a community, supported creator campaigns, or owned organic content as part of a broader marketing role. What matters most is that you can show us you’ve done the work and learned from it.
 Women’s health genuinely interests you. You don’t need to arrive knowing everything about women’s health. But you do need to care enough to learn. We’re talking about real health concerns affecting millions of women, so curiosity, empathy, accuracy, and good judgment matter.
 Bonus points if you’ve worked with Shopify, ecommerce brands, Google Sheets, Jira, Confluence, or similar tools.
 Double bonus points if you already have strong opinions about why most brand TikToks are painfully boring.
 Now, time to be honest… is this really you?
 If you’ve already started thinking about what you’d post first, which competitors you’d stalk, and how you’d build our first 10,000 followers…
 We should probably talk. 
 We don’t expect you to know everything. This isn’t a “12 years of TikTok experience required” job ad. But we do want somebody curious, switched on, commercially minded, organised, and hungry to get very, very good at organic social.
 And someone who sees a brand starting from scratch and thinks:
 Ohhh… this could be fun. 
 Other Qualities You’ll Need
 We’re going to insist that you have these 3 qualities:
 You’re humble — you put the team and others’ needs ahead of your own.
 You’re hungry — you want to learn more, improve, and keep getting better.
 You’re people-smart — in the sense that you’re a great teammate.
 The truth is, if you don’t have these qualities, you won’t last long at our company.
 So if you’re missing one of them, be honest. Save yourself a lot of headaches and skip to a job posting that’s a better fit for you.
 What Will You Earn?
 We believe in rewarding top talent.
 So let’s talk about salary once we’ve had the chance to get to know you better. Rest assured, we’re generous and offer above-market pay for the right person. If you bring the skills, curiosity, and hunger to grow, we’ll make sure the compensation reflects that.
 You’ll also enjoy the following benefits:
 A generous healthcare package
 Monthly team events and activities
 Flexible Stat Holidays with the option to bank days for later use
 Weekly team lunches
 Casual dress code
 An incredible dog-friendly office
 And above all, you’ll join a team that you’ll never want to leave.
 Culture is everything to us.
 Yes, we work extremely hard to change as many people’s lives as possible.
 But we know how to have fun and reward ourselves too.
 How To Apply
 So, do you have what it takes to become the next member of Team AlgaeCal?
 Job opportunities like this don’t come along often, and we’ve got a lot to offer the right person.
 So, to make sure our future Organic Social Specialist is the real deal, will be a great fit, and will thrive here, we ask a little more than your run-of-the-mill job application.
 If this sounds like a position for you, please respond to this advertisement with your resume and cover letter.
 Please read carefully: 
 1. Write a cover letter addressing:
 Why are you the best Organic Social Specialist for this role? Give us examples of accounts, campaigns, or content you’ve worked on — and include results where possible.
 Describe why you fit perfectly with our values. Read them here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1deCCJZ6tiDiOSlr_W0UdCuM_V_ahzPBs/view 
 What’s the toughest challenge you’ve ever overcome in your life? How did you overcome it?
 What are the last three books you’ve read?
 What do you do for fun?
 2. Explain what you’re doing now for a job:
 If you don’t have one, explain why.
 If you have one, explain why you’re looking elsewhere.
 3. Show us what you’ve done.
 Please include links to social accounts, campaigns, posts, videos, or other work you’ve helped create or manage.
 And tell us what you actually did. 
 If something performed particularly well, even better. Give us the numbers.
 4. Upload your cover letter and resume.
 Ensure your cover letter and resume are saved and sent as one file.
 Yes, our hiring process is challenging, but it’s our way of selecting the best — and your way of ensuring your AlgaeCal teammates are tops.
 Click the “Apply Now” button on this page and upload your cover letter and resume. 
 Note: Please include your cover letter WITH your resume in one document. Applications without a cover letter will not be read! 
 We’re looking to hire as soon as we find the right person, so act quickly and you can expect a prompt response.

 Principales responsabilités

 2. Concevoir, rédiger et appliquer des cas d’essai manuels et automatisés qui vérifient la conformité aux exigences fonctionnelles (et certaines non fonctionnelles), d’intégration et de régression.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

About the Role
 You will be the person who makes our AI better at selling. You will read its conversations, notice what is working and what is not, and change the instructions it follows so the next thousand conversations go better.
 You do not need to know everything on day one. We will teach you our tools, our playbooks and how to write and test prompts. What we cannot teach is the instinct for conversations, a feel for sales, and the curiosity to dig into the data and ask why.
 What You'll Do
 Review AI-drafted text messages each day, and approve, edit or rewrite them before they send.
 Spot patterns across conversations, such as an opener that gets replies but no orders, and figure out the cause.
 Update each brand's prompts and playbook to fix problems at the source, then test the change before it goes live.
 Respond to brand requests and turn them into playbook updates.
 Help launch new brands: deep research on their brand, write the persona and opening messages, and check that offers work.
 Run and track A/B tests, and report what won. 
 You read people well. From one text you can tell whether a shopper is ready to buy, has a question, or is done, and you reply the way a real person would.
 You have sales instinct. You answer an objection and then ask for the sale, without arguing or pushing the customer away.
 You are curious about data. You can open a table of conversations and ask the right questions: how many, compared to what, at which brand, since when. You notice when a number looks off and go find out why.
 You fix the cause, not the symptom. When the AI says something wrong, you look for the reason (a missing fact, a vague rule, two rules that conflict) and fix the instruction so it does not happen again.
 You are comfortable with AI tools. You use ChatGPT, Claude or similar tools regularly and understand that how you ask shapes what you get back.
 You are online. These are live conversations. You are responsive during working hours and quick to pick things up in Slack.
 You learn fast and like feedback. You pick up new tools quickly and want to get better each week.
 Nice to Have
 Experience in sales (SDR, BDR, retail or any role with a close rate), customer support, or live chat.
 Experience at a DTC brand or ecommerce agency.
 Familiarity with Shopify, Klaviyo, Postscript or similar tools.
 Spreadsheet skills, or basic SQL.
 Something you have built or automated with AI on your own.
 What We'll Teach You
 Our console, approval queue and playbook system.
 How to write, test and ship prompt changes.
 Shopify basics, discount codes and how they combine.
 How we run and read A/B tests.

 Title of Job : Senior Product Acceleration Specialist - Auth0
 Reports to : Director, Product Acceleration
 Job Purpose
 As a Senior Product Acceleration Specialist for Auth0, you will play a critical role in driving customer success, deep product adoption, and long-term retention across Okta’s most strategic Global 2000 (G2K) enterprise accounts. In this highly technical, developer-centric role, you will act as a trusted advisor to enterprise engineering, architecture, security, and application teams, helping them deploy complex, low-friction, high-volume Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) solutions on the Auth0 platform. 
 Leveraging your deep Auth0 domain knowledge, you will guide customers through their deployment journeys by supporting key architectural decisions, driving optimal platform usage, and troubleshooting complex technical issues. Operating at the intersection of post-sales support, developer enablement, and product innovation, your core focus will include deploying modern front-end frameworks alongside validating New Product Introductions (NPIs). In doing so, you will act as the essential feedback bridge between G2K engineering teams and Auth0’s Product Management.
 Duties & Responsibilities
 Post-Sales Architectural Advisory & Troubleshooting: Partner directly with G2K Enterprise Customers to guide complex implementation patterns, navigate key architectural decisions, and resolve complex configuration challenges to maximize platform capabilities.
 Pre-Sales & NPI Launch Support: Partner with Sales Engineering and Go-To-Market (GTM) teams during the rollout of New Product Introductions (NPIs). Develop high-impact Proof of Concepts (PoCs), early-adopter demonstrations, and technical enablement assets to help secure technical wins and drive initial pipeline for emerging Auth0 capabilities within G2K accounts.
 Developer Enablement & Prototyping: Assist customer development teams by providing architectural guidance on custom Auth0 Actions, SDK implementation blueprints, and modern full-stack application patterns (Node.js, TypeScript, React, Mobile).
 Product & NPI Feedback Loop: Act as a technical liaison between G2K Enterprise Customers and Auth0 Product Management to identify feature gaps, test early-stage NPIs, and drive product roadmap enhancements based on real-world enterprise needs.
 Field & Customer Mentorship: Create reusable code samples, technical documentation, and enablement guides to train G2K teams (Professional Services, Customer Success, Pre-Sales, Partners) and customer developers on advanced Auth0 capabilities.
 AI Tooling & Automation: Leverage AI tools and LLM workflows to accelerate code generation, SDK debugging, technical documentation, and complex implementation analysis.
 Multi-Project Execution: Manage multiple concurrent technical engagements effectively while prioritizing tasks to ensure high customer satisfaction, which includes providing a rapid, hands-on response to high-priority customer escalations and fast-moving GTM activities.
 Qualifications & Technical Requirements
 Experience: 6+ years in a customer-facing technical field role within a Go-To-Market (GTM) organization (e.g., Pre-Sales/Sales Engineering, Professional Services, Solutions Architecture, Technical Account Management, Customer Success, or Senior Support) delivering identity or SaaS solutions to enterprise accounts.
 Auth0 & CIAM Depth: Expert-level understanding of the Auth0 platform and modern Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM) patterns, including low-friction authentication, high-volume user management, and extensibility via custom Auth0 Actions.
 Full-Stack Development Skills: Proven experience reading, writing, and debugging full-stack application code using JavaScript/TypeScript, Node.js, React, and modern Mobile SDKs.
 Identity Protocols & Security: Deep understanding of identity federation, access control frameworks, and core protocols including SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), and SCIM.
 Identity Security & Threat Defense: In-depth knowledge of the CIAM threat landscape, with a proven ability to design and scale resilient authentication flows that mitigate both traditional identity attacks (credential stuffing, account takeover, automated bot attacks, etc.) and emerging next-generation threats (AI-driven social engineering, LLM-based phishing, and automated fraud attacks, etc.)
 G2K Enterprise Experience: Demonstrated history of navigating complex, large-scale IT landscapes, web technologies, and cloud architectures for G2K customers.
 Communication & Advisory: Exceptional ability to translate complex technical/developer concepts to non-technical stakeholders and strategically guide senior engineering leaders.
 Education: A Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related discipline is required.
